27.0.0.en: These verses were mentioned and explained in (2 Kgs 15:33), and in them we see that Jotham became king at the age of twenty-five and reigned sixteen years, and his mother's name was Jerushah the daughter of Zadok. It seems that she was devout, so she brought up her son well, and he walked uprightly.

27.1.0.en: Jotham walked in uprightness and goodness, like his father, but he learned from his father's mistake, so he respected the priesthood and feared God and worshipped Him with reverence. But he was lenient with his people, so he left them to be corrupted by the worship of idols on the high places, that is, he did not remove the high places and the idols on them. Isaiah portrayed this corruption in his prophecy (Isa 1-5), and so did the prophet Micah in his prophecy (1:9, 2:2, 3:8-10, 3:1-2, 5-12).

27.2.0.en: Ophel: A quarter inside Jerusalem lying to its southwest and to the southwest of the temple, and it connects the king's gardens with the temple.

27.2.1.en: Although Jotham did not prevent his people from pagan worship on the high places, he tried in a positive way to draw them to the worship of God, for he took care to build a great gate for the temple, called the higher gate, and by this Jotham fortified the temple.

27.2.2.en: Jotham's concern extended to fortifying Jerusalem, so he built the ruined wall of the city, which was on the side of Ophel.

27.3.0.en: Jotham loved building works, like his father Uzziah, so he took care to build cities in the kingdom of Judah, and he also built towers and fortresses to fortify and protect the city and those in it.

27.4.0.en: A talent of silver: It has several weights, from 17 to 40 kg.

27.4.1.en: Measures (cors): A measure for grain equal to 229 liters. Jotham's strength appeared in his great army, and God helped him because of his uprightness, so he fought the children of Ammon, who dwell east of his kingdom, and triumphed over them and subdued them, so that they paid him a great tribute, whose value was a hundred talents of silver, as well as ten thousand measures of wheat and ten thousand of barley. And the Ammonites continued to pay him this tribute annually for two more years.

27.5.0.en: Jotham reached this strength in his building works and his wars because he walked uprightly before the Lord.

27.5.1.en: If you please God by your upright conduct, He blesses you and makes your works prosper and protects you from the wars of the devil, so He gives you victory over him and you live in peace.

27.5.3.en: 7- Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all his wars, and his ways, lo, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

27.5.4.en: 8- He was five and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. 9- And Jotham slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David: and Ahaz his son reigned in his stead. These verses were mentioned and explained in (2 Kgs 15:36, 38), and in them we see the death of Jotham and his burial in the city of David, and then the reign of Ahaz his son.

27.5.5.en: However great a position a person holds on earth, he will leave it by death. Therefore take care to prepare for your eternal life, by keeping God's commandments and doing good, so that you may have a great place in heaven.

28.0.s.en: (1) Ahaz's corruption and his defeat before Aram and Israel

28.0.0.en: These verses were mentioned and explained in (2 Kgs 16:1-4), and in them we see Ahaz's corruption, his abandoning the worship of God and his immersion in the worship of idols.

28.1.0.en: Ahaz fell into the worship of idols without any cause, because his father was upright and left him much money in the treasury of the kingdom, since he had triumphed over the surrounding enemies, such as the children of Ammon. Therefore God abandoned Ahaz and let the king of Aram attack him and kill many of his people, because they too had gone astray after the king in the worship of idols.

28.1.1.en: God also permitted the king of Israel to attack him and kill many of his people and take many captives.

28.1.2.en: What is mentioned in (2 Kgs 16:5, 6), that the king of Aram and the king of Israel did not overcome Ahaz, means that they wanted to depose and kill him and appoint another king instead of him, but they were not able to do so, yet they killed many of his people. And God did not permit the deposing of Ahaz, because He had promised that a descendant of David would remain on his throne forever. And He sent Isaiah to Ahaz and reassured him that God would keep him (Isa 7).

28.2.0.en: Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, killed a great number of the mighty soldiers of Ahaz, numbering 120,000, because of the kingdom of Judah's walking in evil.

28.3.0.en: And Zichri, the commander of the army of Israel, was able to reach the royal palace and kill Maaseiah the son of Ahaz, and he also killed Azrikam, who was over the royal palace, and Elkanah, the second man in the kingdom after Ahaz.

28.3.1.en: Thus God punished Ahaz by the killing of his son and his helpers and a great number of his army, that perhaps he might repent and return to God. And although Ahaz had offered his son as a sacrifice to the idols, here another son of his dies by the sword; for whoever walks in evil will find before him nothing but divine punishment.

28.3.2.en: Do not challenge God by persisting in evil, lest He be angry with you and abandon you, and the demons humiliate you and those around you trouble you. Return to Him with repentance. He is compassionate and will forgive you.

28.4.s.en: (2) Israel's captivity of Judah and its return

28.4.0.en: The army of Israel was able to take captive 200,000 of the people of Judah, men, women and children, and they plundered much spoil from them. Thus Judah was humbled because of its sins. And although Ahaz had admired the pagan gods whom Israel worshipped and followed them in the worship of idols, now God stirs up the king of Israel against him, to kill and take captive many of his people, in order to teach him not to follow sinners or imitate them in their sins.

28.5.0.en: God's compassion appears toward the inhabitants of the kingdom of Judah, who had rebelled against Him by worshipping idols. For after the kingdom of Israel took them captive, He sent a prophet named Oded to the capital of Israel, which is Samaria, to meet the army of Israel returning with the captives of Judah and its spoil, and he declared to them the following:

28.5.1.en: 1- God disciplined the inhabitants of Judah for their sins, so they were defeated in the war before Israel.

28.5.2.en: 2- The prophet Oded reminded Israel that they had many sins, and that God was longsuffering toward them, but He would abandon them and discipline them if they did not repent; so how could they take captives and spoil from their brethren, the inhabitants of Judah?

28.5.3.en: 3- If Israel had many sins, let it have compassion on its brethren of Judah, sinners like itself, and return their captives to their land.

28.6.0.en: The inhabitants of Samaria were moved by the words of Oded and felt their sins and returned to God. So four of the chiefs of Israel rose up, followed by the people, and spoke to the heads of the army who were returning to Samaria with the captives, and reminded them that Israel had many sins which deserved the divine wrath, so it was not right for us to add to them a new sin, which is cruelty to our brethren the people of Judah, by taking them captive to Israel.

28.6.1.en: This turning and submission to God is a matter that gladdens God, so that He took care to mention the names of the four chiefs in the Holy Bible, though they are not mentioned except in this place. It resembles the goodness shown by the good Samaritan in the parable told by Christ (Lk 10:29-37). For God does not forget the goodness and service of any person, and He cares for everyone who obeys Him and bears witness to Him, especially among the wicked.

28.7.0.en: The heads of the army obeyed the chiefs of Israel, so they left before them the captives from Judah and all their spoil.

28.8.0.en: The chiefs of Israel appointed a number of the people of Israel to care for the captives, and this care appeared in the following:

28.8.1.en: 1- They took clothes from the spoil and clothed the naked captives.

28.8.2.en: 2- They took suitable sandals from the spoil and put them on all the captives.

28.8.3.en: 3- They gave them food and drink, because they had been hungry and thirsty for some time.

28.8.4.en: 4- They cared for the wounds which had afflicted them while they were being seized, or beaten, and while being dragged and carried to Samaria, so they anointed their wounds with oil that they might heal.

28.8.5.en: 5- They cared for those of them who were weary and unable to walk, and set them on donkeys, so that they would not fall on the way back to their country.

28.8.6.en: 6- They led them with gentleness and love and looked after them during their journey, until they brought them to the city of Jericho, which is called the city of palm trees, a city lying in the north of the kingdom of Judah.

28.8.7.en: In these steps we see wonderful care on the part of the Samaritans, which resembles, as we said, what the good Samaritan did.

28.8.8.en: Be merciful and have compassion on the weary around you, because your tenderness toward them is very precious in the sight of God, and He pours out His mercies upon you.

28.9.s.en: (3) Ahaz's brokenness before Edom, Philistia and Assyria

28.9.0.en: After Ahaz's crushing defeat before Aram and Israel, he did not think of returning to God, but tried to seek the help of a great state, Assyria, which dwells in the north of present-day Iraq, to help him against Aram and all the enemies around him. This shows the extent of Ahaz's hardness of heart and his distance from God.

28.10.0.en: God continued His discipline of the hard-hearted Ahaz, so He permitted Edom, who dwells south of Judah, to attack Ahaz, and it triumphed over him and took captives from him.

28.11.0.en: Beth-shemesh: A city in the north of the kingdom of Judah and on its border.

28.11.1.en: Ajalon: A city on the border of the kingdom of Judah in its north, lying west of Jerusalem at a distance of 22 km. Gederoth: A city in the plain of Judah.

28.11.2.en: Shocho: A city in the plain of Judah, lying southwest of Bethlehem, at a distance of 14 miles. Timnah: A city lying on the northern border of Judah, 5 km southwest of Beth-shemesh. Gimzo: A village lying southeast of Lydda at a distance of 5 km.

28.11.3.en: God also permitted the Philistines to attack the kingdom of Judah from its south and its north, and they seized a number of its cities.

28.12.0.en: Made Judah unruly: He made Judah rebel against God.

28.12.1.en: Ahaz led his people in rebellion against God and made them wander in the worship of idols, so God permitted him and his people to be disciplined, and humbled him before the nations around him. For after he became weak before Aram and Israel, the other nations around Ahaz, such as Edom and Philistia, seized the opportunity, so they attacked him and seized his cities and took captives from him. In all this Ahaz did not repent and take refuge in God, but sought the nations and their gods, such as Assyria.

28.13.0.en: Then, in continuation of God's humbling of Ahaz, He permitted Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, whom Ahaz had tried to enlist for help, but who did not support him, to attack him and humble him, although he had taken from Ahaz many gifts, from the house of the Lord, from the king's palace and from the princes of Judah. And because Ahaz stripped the house of the Lord of its contents and gave them as gifts to the king of Assyria, the king of Assyria did not help him, but increased his humiliation and weakness.

28.13.1.en: Do not take refuge in the world, lest it humble you, but seek God your compassionate Father, because however much you sin, He is ready to forgive you as long as you return to Him. Leave the means of the world, its lusts and wrong ways, to save your soul from perishing.

28.14.s.en: (4) Ahaz's worship of the gods of Assyria and his death

28.14.0.en: Although affliction calls man to return to God, when God permitted affliction to come upon Ahaz, he drew away from God and clung to the nations and their idols.

28.15.0.en: In Ahaz's persistence in his evil, he took refuge in the gods of Aram, who had smitten and humbled him, and did not take refuge in God. He feared the gods of Aram and sought their help, although God is the greatest power in the world, but in his ignorance Ahaz rejected God.

28.16.0.en: Ahaz cut in pieces the large vessels which were in the house of the Lord, to send them as metal gifts to Assyria, and he shut up the house of the Lord and prevented service in it. He most likely shut up the sanctuary and the Holy of Holies, that is, he prevented the priests from entering and offering service to God, because he had set up an altar for the idols, like what he had seen in Damascus among the Arameans; that is, he prevented the worship of God and encouraged the worship of idols, and moreover he set up altars for the idols in every corner of the city of Jerusalem.

28.16.1.en: Persisting in sin blinds a person's eyes, so that he departs from the truth. Therefore be careful to pray, to read the Holy Bible and to receive Holy Communion, so that your relationship with God may remain alive.

28.17.0.en: Likewise Ahaz established the worship of idols in the cities of Judah, and not in Jerusalem only, and by this he provoked God and greatly angered Him, because he led his people astray and led them far from God.

28.17.1.en: Thus we see Ahaz's evil in that he spread the worship of idols, set up the high places and shut up the house of God. He was not merely lenient with his people in the worship of idols, but encouraged them in this wicked worship and drew them away from God.

28.18.0.en: These two verses were mentioned and explained in (2 Kgs 16:19, 20), and in them we see the end of the wicked Ahaz, who was buried after his death in Jerusalem, and not in the tombs of the righteous kings, his predecessors. The beginning of the revival of King Hezekiah, his reforms and his great works

29.0.s.en: (2) The call to the priests and Levites

29.0.0.en: Hezekiah began his reforms by repairing the house of the Lord and opening its doors, so that service could be offered in it. His father Ahaz had shut the doors of the house and set up an altar after the pattern of the idols' altar which he had seen in Damascus (2 Kgs 16:10, 11), and had neglected the worship of God.

29.0.1.en: The repairing of the doors of the house of the Lord means overlaying them with gold, which Hezekiah afterwards stripped off to give to the king of Assyria (2 Kgs 18:16). Hezekiah's goodness appears here in that, at the beginning of his reign, in the first month of the first year of his reign, he began to take care of the house of the Lord, because the beginning of every good thing comes from man's relationship with the Church.

29.0.2.en: May your attachment to the Holy Sacraments and your relationship with the Church be the center of your life and the most important thing in it, and organize all your concerns so that they do not encroach upon your relationship with the Church and your service in it.

29.1.0.en: King Hezekiah gathered the priests and Levites in the east court of the house of the Lord. These are the servants of the temple who know God's Law and His worship; therefore Hezekiah relied on them to begin his reform by renewing the worship in the temple. And he asked two things of them:

29.1.1.en: 1- That they sanctify themselves, in order to purify their hearts by repentance, and also to complete the procedures of the Law concerning purification, so that they would be worthy to serve the house of the Lord.

29.1.2.en: 2- After they had sanctified themselves, Hezekiah asked them to sanctify the house of the Lord, by the following:

29.1.3.en: a- Removing the traces of pagan worship.

29.1.4.en: b- Carrying out a general cleaning, to remove the dust and every remnant of neglect, so that the house of the Lord might be in the most beautiful condition, befitting His great presence.

29.2.0.en: Hezekiah comes forward in a spirit of repentance, confessing the sins of the fathers, who were unfaithful to God. For Moses, and after him Joshua, and also Jehoiada the priest, who lived in the days of King Joash, made a covenant, on behalf of the people, with God, that they would live with Him and keep His commandments. But the people of God, whether in the kingdom of Judah in the days of Ahaz, the father of Hezekiah, and the kings before him, or in the kingdom of Israel, had forsaken God and worshipped idols and walked in their evil lusts.

29.3.0.en: In the fathers' neglect of God, they abandoned His worship in His house; for example, the shutting of the porch, in which the people who came to worship God gathered, and the priests also neglected the service in the sanctuary, whether in lighting the lamps in the lampstands, or in offering incense on the golden altar of incense. As for the bronze altar before the sanctuary, they no longer offered burnt offerings to God upon it. Thus the house of God became as though abandoned, lifeless and dark, because they were occupied with the worship of idols.

29.4.0.en: Hezekiah reminds the priests and Levites, the religious leaders of the people, that when the fathers in the kingdom of Judah forsook God and worshipped idols, God permitted the nations around them, such as Assyria and Aram and the kingdom of Israel, to trouble them, so they were in anxiety and confusion, until the surrounding nations marveled at their weakness.

29.5.0.en: Hezekiah also warns those gathered with him about what happened in the kingdom of Israel, for the Assyrians attacked it and took it into captivity, and the kingdom of Israel came to an end in the days of Ahaz, the father of Hezekiah, since the captivity was in the year 722 B.C., at the end of the reign of Ahaz; that is, only a short time had passed since the captivity when Hezekiah began to reign. Here appears Hezekiah's confession that the cause of all the afflictions that came upon the people of God was their sins. By all this Hezekiah tries to warn the servants of the temple and encourage them, to obtain God's pleasure by being exact in His worship, and to save themselves from God's punishment, which took place in the days of the fathers.

29.6.0.en: In the end Hezekiah showed his clear intention to make a covenant with God, to live before Him with all his heart, keeping His commandments and holding fast to His Law, so that he might escape the divine wrath. And as a leader he encourages his people by this covenant to follow him and worship God.

29.7.0.en: This verse shows the fatherhood of Hezekiah, who was still young in age, for he was twenty-five years old, but he bore a great heart and the responsibility of a king for his people, so he says to them, "My sons," and asks the priests and Levites to take care of their service in the temple, since God chose them from among the people to offer the sacrifices and burnt offerings and to light the lamps and incense before Him.

29.8.s.en: (3) The Levites' cleansing of the temple

29.8.0.en: The chiefs of the three Levite clans were zealous: the Kohathites, the Merarites and the Gershonites. Two from each clan rose up, in addition to two from each of the four clans of the singers: Elizaphan, Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun, so the total was fourteen chiefs. And in honor of them God mentioned each one of them by name in the Holy Bible, because they were moved by Hezekiah's words and were zealous for the service of the house of the Lord.

29.8.1.en: God notices your love and your care for His worship and service, and all that you do is of great value before Him, however small it may seem in your eyes. This is your opportunity at this age to express your love for Him, after He expressed His love for you on the Cross, and even prepared the Kingdom for you, that you may rejoice with Him forever.

29.9.0.en: These chiefs felt that Hezekiah's words were based on God's word in His Law given to Moses; therefore they were zealous at once and gathered their brethren the Levites to cleanse the temple.

29.10.0.en: The brook Kidron: A valley lying southeast of Jerusalem, into which the corpses and refuse coming out of the city used to be thrown and burned there, and it joins the valley of the son of Hinnom, in which a fire burns continually, and from it the word "Gehenna" is taken.

29.10.1.en: The priests cleansed and cleaned the sanctuary, where none is permitted to enter except the priests. And they brought out all uncleanness and filth to the court of the house of God, where the Levites stand, and they took all the uncleanness, with what they had gathered from the court of the house of the Lord, and carried it to the brook Kidron, where they burned it.

29.11.0.en: The cleansing of the sanctuary took eight days, from the first day of the first month of Hezekiah's reign to the eighth day; and the cleansing of the court of the house of the Lord and the porch took another eight days, and the carrying of the uncleanness in it to the brook Kidron took another eight days; that is, the cleansing of the house of the Lord and all that is connected with it was completed in sixteen days. This shows the abundance of the uncleanness that was there and the extreme neglect in the days of Ahaz and those before him. On the other hand, it shows the care of the priests and Levites for cleansing the house of the Lord.

29.12.0.en: After the house of the Lord was cleansed, the chiefs of the priests and Levites entered and announced to King Hezekiah the completion of the cleansing of the house of the Lord and everything in it, whether the altars, or the vessels used in them, and everything that was in the sanctuary and in the court of the house of the Lord.

29.13.0.en: The young Hezekiah inherited a poor, tattered kingdom far from God, but he did not give up; rather he rose with energy to bring his kingdom back to God. King Hezekiah's love for God appears in that he rose early, because the longings of his heart drove him to pray in the house of the Lord, so he gathered the rulers of his people in his kingdom of Judah and went up to the house of the Lord, because it was built on a hill inside Jerusalem.

29.14.0.en: Hezekiah was not content with cleansing the house of the Lord, but also took care to sanctify it and to make atonement for the people, by offering sacrifices for himself and for his people. This shows that Hezekiah was not content with grieving over the wrong, but did a positive work to correct the wrongs.

29.14.1.en: And Hezekiah commanded the priests to offer seven each of bulls, rams, lambs and he goats for the sins of all the people, although the Law provides for offering one bull as a burnt offering (Num 15:24) and one he goat as a sin offering (Lev 16:15). Perhaps Hezekiah felt the greatness of his sins and those of his people, because they had neglected to offer sacrifices for many years in the days of his fathers, who neglected the worship of God; therefore he offered the number seven of the animals. And the number seven represents perfection, since Hezekiah felt the perfection of their sin; therefore he needed a complete atonement.

29.14.2.en: And when Hezekiah says that these sacrifices are for the kingdom, he means his kingdom, that is, the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and by the sanctuary he means the house of the Lord and all that is in it, while by Judah he means all the people of God; for in the Septuagint Israel is written instead of Judah, that is, he means the people of the two kingdoms, because Hezekiah felt his responsibility for his people who were far away in the kingdom of Israel, who had been scattered in the Assyrian captivity, while the weak among them remained in their cities.

29.15.0.en: The priests killed the seven bulls, and likewise the rams and the lambs, as burnt offerings before God, and sprinkled their blood on the bronze altar, upon which they offered them. Thus the altar regained its place and burnt offerings went up upon it to please God.

29.16.0.en: The priests laid their hands on the seven he goats of the sin offering, declaring, on behalf of the people, their sin before God, their neglect of His worship and their disobedience of His commandments, and this was before the king and the people. Then they killed these goats and offered them on the bronze altar, to make atonement for the sins of all the people of God, whether in the kingdom of Judah, or the remnant of the northern kingdom of Israel, or those scattered in captivity, because the Assyrian captivity took place in the days of his father King Ahaz. And Hezekiah is the first king since the division of the kingdom to care for the salvation, not only of the people of his kingdom of Judah, but of the people of all the tribes, and to offer sacrifices for them.

29.17.0.en: After Hezekiah had cleansed the house of the Lord and sanctified it and offered the sacrifices to make atonement for the people, he was able to arrange the priests and the Levite singers, and they stood in the house of the Lord with the musical instruments to sing the Psalms, as King David and Gad the seer and Nathan the prophet had commanded and arranged. For Hezekiah took care of the order of worship which he had received and which had come down to him from the days of King David, and this shows the importance of holding fast to the holy Tradition, that is, the oral teachings which have come down to us from the days of the Apostles, and all the rites of the Church.

29.17.1.en: And we see clearly that after offering repentance and obtaining forgiveness, a person can launch out into the praise of God and enjoy His presence.

29.18.0.en: While the burnt offering was being offered, the singers praised God, and the people worshipped before Him, and the king stood in joy and glorification of God.

29.18.1.en: Thus Hezekiah restored the rite which the Lord commanded in the days of Moses, which is the offering of the burnt offering morning and evening every day.

29.19.0.en: After the offering of the sacrifice, the king and all the people bowed down in submission to God and in declaration of their holding fast to His worship, and he promised them that they would live for Him. All this was with the praises raised by the singers, in thanksgiving to God, who gave them the grace of standing before Him.

29.19.1.en: How beautiful it is for you to be in the Church and take part in the prayers and praises and receive the Holy Mysteries, for it is the greatest thing in existence. Be careful of this, whatever your problems, for this is the pledge of the Kingdom and your help in this life, that you may succeed in all your works.

29.20.0.en: You have filled your hands to the Lord: You have been sanctified and consecrated to the service of God, after being far from it for many years, and it may be that some of the priests had not begun their service, because they found no opportunity for the priesthood in the days of the former wicked kings.

29.20.1.en: Of a free heart: A heart full of love for God.

29.20.2.en: After the people saw the sacrifices which Hezekiah offered, mentioned in (v. 21), they were encouraged to offer sacrifices to God themselves also, especially after Hezekiah announced to them that the priests had sanctified themselves and begun their priestly work. So they offered sacrifices and thank offerings to God, who gave them the grace of worshipping Him in His house, and everyone whose heart was full of love offered burnt offerings to God; for burnt offerings are burned entirely before God and the one who offers them takes nothing of them, and this signifies that everyone whose heart is filled with the love of God is ready to give his whole life to Him. Thus the importance of example appears, for the people learned from Hezekiah, who offered the sacrifices and rose early to the house of the Lord.

29.20.3.en: Be assured that your good works and your conduct as a child of God affect those around you more than any words. So worship God with all your heart and offer your love to those around you, for your life is the Gospel lived out, which proclaims Christ to those around you.

29.21.0.en: The number of the sacrifices offered as burnt offerings, that is, burned entirely to God, was large: seventy bulls, a hundred rams and two hundred lambs. This shows that a great number of the people had their hearts filled with the love of God, as we mentioned in (v. 31).

29.22.0.en: And the rest of the sacrifices, besides the burnt offerings, were six hundred oxen and three thousand sheep, and this is a large number which shows the people's turning to repentance and the worship of God.

29.23.0.en: The number of the priests was small, perhaps because of King Hezekiah's quick beginning in cleansing the house of the Lord and sanctifying it, for some of the priests hastened to come to Jerusalem and purify themselves in preparation for service, while the rest delayed. But the Levites were quicker in responding to the call of King Hezekiah, for they were more upright and more concerned with renewing the service in the house of the Lord. Therefore, because of the abundance of the sacrifices and the fewness of the priests, the priests needed the Levites' help in flaying the sacrifices, so that they might offer them on the bronze altar before God.

29.24.0.en: Although King Hezekiah's command was sudden for the priests and Levites and all the people, that they should hasten to cleanse and sanctify the temple and restore the worship in it, the Spirit of the Holy God moved the hearts of many of the people, so they came and offered sacrifices and rejoiced at the return of worship in the holy temple.

29.24.1.en: The restoration of the feasts of the Passover and Unleavened Bread: King Hezekiah, at the beginning of his reign, took care of matters that show his goodness, which are:

29.24.2.en: 1- In the first month he took care to cleanse and sanctify the temple and to offer sacrifices, and these signify repentance and the examination of the soul.

29.24.3.en: 2- In the second month he called for the keeping of the Passover, which is one of the important feasts, which signify Christ the Redeemer, and all the people keep it, and it signifies partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord.
